This is actually quite a hard question when you think about it. One of the issues that I have is that some games are so much like movies already that actually making a movie based on it would be redundant. IMHO The film ought not have the feeling of just being an extended cut scene of a game. To use the example of the Final Fantasy movie, which I think fell into this trap. Which is ironic because I think most people who actually play games tend to hate things that detract from the gameplay experience like cut scenes or pre-scripted events. Even if some people must like them due to the fact that games like this still seem to sell.

Then there is the problem is that games tend to not have good central characters by design. In the context of a game this works because it's normally up to the player to inject their own personality into the game - even to the extent of being able to customize their appearance - but this is just not something that's going to work in movies. When you think about it what do you actually know about the character of Master Chief or Gordon Freeman? For example a lot of games tend to have protagonists that are completely silent or have minimal personality which is something that I think just isn't going to work in the context of movies. Sure some games might have strong supporting characters like GlaDos but if the central character is just a mute it's just going to kill any potential narrative, right there.

In addition to this there is the added complication that games can be heavily influenced by other media as well. I would place The Last of Us, and Rockstar games under this category. This isn't necessarily a bad thing since everything is a copy of a remake of a copy nowadays but I think that there still needs to be a test as to far some games "own" their own universe, and some games just do this better than others IMHO, For example Mass Effect seems heavily influenced by Babylon 5, IMHO. It's that whole good artist borrow but great artists steal argument. Or how quickly the IP gets compared to another IP,

So - in my mind - under these tests, a good potential game to movie adaptations would be ones that are based on games that are not heavily narratively focused already, I.E., cut scene based, has a strong central character and are based in a original universe. Consequently my short list would be:

i, Deus Ex - Human Revolution ii, God of War. iii, Mirror's Edge.
